forces.title: Erosion of 'evergreen' banking relationships with CIB clients.
forces.description: CIB client relationships are fundamentally changing from guaranteed to continuously contested. Corporates, institutional investors, and financial sponsors now annually reassess and reallocate significant portions of their banking wallet (12-25%). This structural shift means investment banks and brokers cannot rely on historical ties; they must actively compete for mandates based on performance, pricing, and service in areas like M&A, capital markets, and flow products, intensifying competition.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Increased wallet share volatility driven by institutional investors and sponsors.
forces.description: Institutional investors and financial sponsors exhibit higher volatility in banking wallet reallocation compared to corporates, moving 17% and up to 25% respectively per cycle. This dynamism creates significant upside for investment banks and brokers who can consistently offer best available pricing, novel ideas, and optimal structural terms on a deal-by-deal basis. Proactive, actionable outreach and highly targeted niche capabilities are key to capturing these shifting mandates, enhancing deal volumes and market share.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Corporate strategic rebalancing to prevent single-provider dependency.
forces.description: Corporates engage in strategic rebalancing of their banking wallet, consciously shifting mandates to diversify providers and prevent over-reliance on a single institution. This behavior creates a headwind for incumbent investment banks, as even strong relationships are subject to reallocation to ensure competitive tension and mitigate risk. Investment banks must therefore continuously demonstrate value beyond core operational services to retain a significant share of high-value mandates like M&A and capital markets.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Consolidation of high-yield mandates to 'anchor' investment banks.
forces.description: CIB clients, particularly corporates, consolidate high-yield, complex mandates (such as global liquidity, FX, M&A, and capital markets) with their primary 'anchor' banks. This presents a significant upside for investment banks capable of achieving anchor status, as it leads to a disproportionately larger share of wallet (up to three times more). Strategic differentiation, optimized coverage models, and tailored products are crucial for securing these lucrative relationships and increasing deal volumes.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Shift in CIB client selection criteria beyond price to execution certainty.
forces.description: CIB clients are increasingly prioritizing execution certainty and operational reliability alongside pricing when selecting investment banking and lending providers. For M&A and complex financing, the ability to flawlessly execute major milestones and maintain efficient processes is highly valued. This structural shift demands that investment banks invest in robust operational capabilities and a proven track record to secure mandates, fostering trust-based relationships as a key competitive advantage that can impact deal flows and market share.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Growing demand for specialized private-capital services from institutional investors.
forces.description: As institutional investors increase their allocation to alternative assets, there is a rising demand for investment banks offering specialized private-capital services. These include capital-call financing, secondary market solutions, syndication, and co-investment facilitation. Banks with deep sector expertise and a strong performance track record in these niche areas are better positioned to capture mandates and wallet share from these valuable clients, creating a significant upside opportunity for specialized investment banking teams.

viewpoints.title: CIB client relationships are no longer guaranteed, requiring continuous re-earning.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's CIB survey reveals that client relationships are no longer evergreen, with significant wallet share contested annually across segments. Corporates reallocate 12-13% of their wallet, institutional investors 17%, and financial sponsors up to 25% per cycle. Investment banks and brokers must actively re-earn this contestable share, especially in flow and event products like M&A and financing, rather than relying on historical ties. Prioritizing service and proactive delivery is crucial to maintaining client relationships and capturing mandates.
viewpoints.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

viewpoints.title: Achieving 'anchor bank' status significantly boosts wallet share from CIB clients.
viewpoints.description: Becoming a primary or 'anchor' bank offers substantial benefits for investment banking and brokerage firms, consolidating up to three times more wallet share from corporate, institutional investor, and financial sponsor clients. Corporates allocate around 73% of their wallet to primary banks, while institutional investors and financial sponsors commit 60% and 55% respectively. This status is achieved by providing high-yield, complex mandates in areas like M&A and capital markets, and strategically competing with optimized coverage and differentiated products.
viewpoints.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

viewpoints.title: Beyond price, execution certainty and strong relationships differentiate CIB providers.
viewpoints.description: While pricing remains a leading factor for CIB clients selecting financing and lending providers, execution certainty and the strength of the banking relationship are equally critical differentiators for investment banks. Corporates value operational reliability for major milestones like mergers and efficient processes. Institutional investors seek sector expertise and innovative private-capital solutions. Financial sponsors prioritize execution track record and certainty in deal closing. Banks must build trust-based relationships and demonstrate exceptional delivery to secure anchor status and repeat mandates, offering a stronger competitive advantage than product features or price alone.

demand_drivers.description: Large-scale corporate events such as mergers, capital restructuring, and new investments trigger significant wallet rotation, driving demand for investment banking services and allowing clients to shift mandates based on best performance and structural terms.

These products are frequently retendered by corporate clients to the most competitive provider based on pricing and execution, leading to constant shifts in wallet allocation for related services provided by investment banks and brokers.

Private equity and venture capital firms dynamically shift mandates to maximize transaction value, selecting investment banking providers based on deal size, product suitability, and specific niche capabilities for complex financing structures and advisory services.

new_opportunities.description: Consolidating a primary relationship with CIB clients can lead to disproportionately higher wallet share (up to three times more), providing opportunities for high-yield, complex mandates in global liquidity, FX, M&A, and capital markets for investment banks.

Institutional investors increasingly allocate assets to alternatives, creating demand for investment banks demonstrating expertise in private-capital services like capital-call financing, secondary market solutions, syndication, and co-investment facilitation.

Beyond competitive pricing, delivering execution certainty for major milestones (e.g., mergers), operational reliability, and fostering strong, trust-based relationships provide a significant competitive advantage to secure and retain mandates from CIB clients for investment banking services.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of Corporate and Investment Banking (CIB) client wallet allocation dynamics based on a global survey of over 300 corporations, institutional investors, and financial sponsors. The study quantifies the annual reallocation of wallet share (12-25%) and the concentration of business with primary banks (55-73%), focusing on competitive behavior and opportunities rather than overall market size for investment banking and brokerage services.
